prompt: Write part of a deposition transcript (about 400 words) of a plaintiff in a car accident lawsuit. The defense lawyer asks (lines start with 'Q:') and the plaintiff answers (lines start with 'A:'). Accident: low-speed head-on collision in League City, Texas. Injury: shoulder injury. Ask about the accident, treatment and daily life. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1481; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather just say I'm the plaintiff in this case. I'm not going to give my full name on this recording, so you'll have to work with what's already on the file.

Q: Understood. Let's move on. Can you describe how the collision happened?

A: I was driving home on a weekday afternoon. The traffic was light, and I was in my lane heading the usual direction when a car crossed the center line and hit me nearly head-on. It was not a high-speed crash. I remember the airbag didn't go off, and both cars were still drivable enough to pull to the shoulder before the police arrived.

Q: How fast do you believe you were traveling at the time of impact?

A: Maybe twenty-five miles an hour, maybe a little less. I'd been braking for a slow vehicle ahead of me, so I wasn't moving quickly.

Q: Did you feel any pain at the scene?

A: Not right away. I was shaken up and my neck felt stiff, but I thought I'd just been jolted. The shoulder started hurting that evening, and by the next morning I could barely lift my arm above my waist.

Q: Who did you first see for treatment?

A: I went to an urgent care clinic the following day. They took x-rays, ruled out a fracture, and gave me a sling and some anti-inflammatory pills. After about two weeks they referred me to an orthopedic specialist.

Q: What did the specialist recommend?

A: Physical therapy, three times a week at first, then less often. They also gave me an injection. The therapist had me doing stretches at home, and I still do those most mornings.

Q: Since the accident, have you missed any work?

A: A few days in the first month, and I had to leave early on several afternoons because I couldn't sit at my desk for long. My job involves a lot of typing and filing, so the shoulder made everything harder.

Q: How has the injury affected your daily life outside of work?

A: I can't do the things I used to. I garden, and I haven't been able to do that properly this season. Carrying groceries is hard, and I've stopped playing tennis on weekends. Sleeping is difficult because I often wake up when I roll onto that side.

Q: Do you still have pain today?

A: Yes, it's better than it was, but it flares up when I lift anything heavy or reach overhead. Some days are much worse than others.
